newsitem.title: EGYPT: Shorouk Air to seek new Airbus 320 next year.
newsitem.headline: Shorouk Air to seek new Airbus 320 next year.

text.p: Shorouk Air, making profits after years in the red, may order a new Airbus 320 in the first four months of next year, the company chairman said on Tuesday.
"If a feasibility study shows it is worth adding a new plane in light of making profits, we will order a new Airbus 320 between January and April 1997," chairman Mahmoud el-Serafi told Reuters.
To minimise operating costs, the plane and engines will be of the same type as those the company already has, Serafi said. The airline has two Airbus 320s.
The company will ask for delivery to be in the summer of 1997, he added.
The company, which has capital of $50 million, was founded in 1992 as a 51-49 percent joint venture between EgyptAir and Kuwait Airways.
After a total loss of $25 million over the last two years, the company has made a profit of $900,000 so far this year, Serafi said.
